hypotheses.claim: The 'shadowed binding' bail-out in get_delegated_event (Attribute.js ~line 209) incorrectly fires when the callback declares its own local variable with the same name as an outer binding: scope.get on the function's metadata scope resolves to the local const, while context.state.scope resolves to the outer each binding, so local_binding.node !== binding.node and hoisting is refused even though the callback never reads the outer binding.
evidence_refs: baseline failure ARE_EXPECTED_HOISTED_CALLBACK for button_1 (shadowed const index) while unshadowed C is hoisted
hypotheses.falsifier: Patching the bail-out to skip when the resolved binding is declared inside the target function makes B compile as a shared/hoisted identifier while C stays hoisted and other cases (true shadowing of outer reads) remain unhoisted.
hypotheses.prediction: Adding a check that binding.scope is within target_function.metadata.scope before bailing will let B's handler be hoisted, matching C.

hypotheses.claim: The bail-out is correct and instead the EachBlock index check (binding.initial?.type === 'EachBlock') or reference bookkeeping is what blocks B, e.g. references are collected per-name and the local const index is confused with the each index binding during the each-index bail.
hypotheses.falsifier: If the each-index check were the blocker, C (which references no each binding) would pass but any handler referencing the each index would also be blocked — but B does not reference the each binding at all (its 'index' resolves to the local const), so the each-index check cannot fire for B; instrumenting would show the shadow bail fires first.
hypotheses.prediction: Removing/altering the each-index check would not change B's output; only the shadow check matters.
